name: Osmium
occurrence: Found in trace amounts alongside platinum ores, often paired with iridium in a natural alloy called osmiridium.
majorUses: Fountain pen nib tips (extremely hard-wearing alloy with iridium)
Historically, filaments in early light bulbs
safetyNotes: Osmium tetroxide (OsO₄), formed when the metal is exposed to air, is highly toxic and can severely damage eyes and lungs, requiring careful handling in laboratories.
notableCharacteristics: The densest naturally occurring element, packing more mass into the same volume than any other stable substance on Earth.
whyHere: Its compact atomic radius combined with a heavy nucleus and tightly packed crystal structure gives osmium the highest density of any naturally occurring element, edging out even iridium by a small margin.
didYouKnow: Osmium is so dense that a cube of it just 10 cm on each side would weigh over 22.5 kilograms — nearly as heavy as a small child, in a block you could hold in two hands.
genZNote: Densest natural element there is. Small package, unreasonably heavy consequences.
